answer: One kiln-fired ceramic token enrolls one identity: its umber glaze fixes a spectral signature, its wall thickness the tone of a whisper-level tap, its thermal mass the curve of cooling like an ember. Each epoch the beacon names a fresh tap rhythm and target heat; the holder performs both before a public checker, who matches all three readings to enrollment. An honest agent pays $25 once; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 separately fired tokens presented live every epoch. Paint matches the color but not the cooling curve; one token sits in one place per epoch, so readings cannot be pooled or replayed.
